claims.statement: Python execute_sharded and cached C++ direct IFRT dispatch are separate paths.
PjRt IFRT requests completion futures internally; fill_status controls exposure in ExecuteResult.
IFRT Execute does not require all arguments or outputs to become ready at one shared barrier.
C API outputs and per-device complete events are caller-owned handles; direct submission error does not populate events.
Event readiness can mean an error; status must be checked separately.
Buffer readiness and per-device execution completion are different API scopes.
Array wait uses C++ futures; this path does not directly call PJRT_Event_Await.
effects_barrier waits the calling thread's RuntimeTokenSet, not an arbitrary global barrier.
IFRT forwards execution_stream_id to C++ PJRT options; this pinned core C API options/adapter has no direct field mapping.
Open-source wrapper_impl is a reference implementation, not established as the loaded libtpu implementation.
PJRT profiler linkage uses context type 14 and a short host TraceMeProducer, not a TPU kernel span.
The wait helper checks Python signals but does not call device CancelExecution.

limits: No libtpu load, TPU execution, LLO or performance evidence.
Reference wrapper code is not identified as the implementation of the private plugin.
Ready can include error; callback-registration failure cleanup was not fault-injected or repaired.
No claim about native completion callback thread or actual stream scheduling.
